newsitem.title: USA: DLJ says underwriting outlook improving.
newsitem.headline: DLJ says underwriting outlook improving.

text.p: Donaldon Lufkin & Jenrette Inc is seeing signs of improvement in its underwriting business after a slow quarter, the company's president said.

Early today, DLJ reported second quarter earnings of $1.54 per share, up slightly from $1.53 a year ago. On a fully diluted basis, earnings per share fell to $1.49 from $1.53, but still topped First Call's consensus estimate of $1.20.

One of the few areas of weakness in the quarter was underwriting, with revenues falling to $164.5 million in the quarter from $255.5 million a year ago, reflecting a much weaker initial public offering market.
But business has picked up of late, company president and chief operating officer Joe Roby said.
"We went through a sinking spell in underwriting," Roby said, "but our calendar and deal activity look better now than they had for the last 90 days.
"Also, we have a big high-yield debt (underwriting) calendar for July and if everything happens that's supposed to, we'll have $3 billion in lead-managed underwritings."

In contrast to the underwriting performance, DLJ saw its fee-based revenues jump to $176.7 million in the quarter from $101.5 million a year ago. The gains came primarily from mergers and acquisitions, private fund capital raising assignments and management fees from merchant banking funds.

"We've significantly improved our standings in M&A over the last 18 months and our private funds group, which raises money for leveraged buyouts, had a spectacular quarter," Roby said. "We're very optimistic for the second half of the year."
Roby declined to comment on expectations for the next two quarters, noting only that "most analysts seem to be raising estimates for the year."
